question: A 28-year-old woman presents to the clinic with complaints of occasional low-grade fever and joint pain for 1 month. She also complains of morning stiffness in the proximal interphalangeal joints of both hands, which lasts for 5 to 10 minutes. She recently noticed a pink rash on her nose and cheekbones. Her family history is significant for similar complaints in her mother. She is not taking any medications. On examination, her temperature is 37.6°C (99.6°F), pulse is 74/min, blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg, and respirations are 18/min. Aphthous ulcers are noted on her oral mucosa. Which of the following tests would be most specific for confirming the diagnosis in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "28-year-old woman" -> "complaints of low-grade fever and joint pain" -> "morning stiffness in proximal interphalangeal joints" -> "pink rash on nose and cheekbones" -> "family history of similar complaints" -> "aphthous ulcers on oral mucosa" -> "clinical features suggestive of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)" -> "consider autoimmune connective tissue disorder" -> 80%
analysis: The patient's presentation with joint pain, low-grade fever, morning stiffness, rash on the nose and cheekbones, and family history of similar complaints suggests a possible diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Among the options provided, the most specific test for confirming the diagnosis of SLE would be the Anti-double stranded DNA (dsDNA) antibodies test, as the presence of these antibodies is highly specific for SLE.
